choices: A nihilating structure that is never coincident with itself, and is therefore condemned to be free
A dense, self-identical thing like a stone (being-in-itself)
A collection of immanent mental contents (noemata) housed within the mind
A ready-to-hand item within a referential totality of equipment
explanation: For Sartre consciousness is being-for-itself: a nihilating structure never simply identical with itself and therefore 'condemned to be free.' Being-in-itself (the dense, self-identical stone) is the mode of things; he rejects immanent noemata housed in the mind; and ready-to-hand equipment is Heidegger's category, not Sartre's account of consciousness.
